title: HB651 (2017-2018 Regular Session): Georgia Firearms and Weapons Act; enact

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk dataset (gun-policy Stage 5 LegiScan check); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official legis.ga.gov PDF of the version named in note (via LegiScan getBillText)

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-121 to 16-11-124), definition: (1) 'Bump fire stock' means any device that replaces or supplements, or is designed to replace or supplement, a weapon's buttstock or pistol grip and enables, or is designed to enable, such weapon to shoot more than six shots by a single function of the trigger or by recoil of the weapon.
SECTION 1 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-121 to 16-11-124), definition: (2)(3) 'Machine gun' means any weapon which: (A) Shoots shoots or is designed to shoot, automatically, more than six shots, without manual reloading, by a single function of the trigger; or (B) Is used with a bump fire stock.
SECTION 1 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-121 to 16-11-124), 16-11-122: No person shall have in his or her possession any sawed-off shotgun, sawed-off rifle, machine gun, dangerous weapon, bump fire stock, or silencer except as provided in Code Section 16-11-124.
SECTION 1 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-121 to 16-11-124), 16-11-123: A person commits the offense of unlawful possession of firearms or weapons when he or she knowingly has in his or her possession any sawed-off shotgun, sawed-off rifle, machine gun, dangerous weapon, bump fire stock, or silencer, and, upon conviction thereof, he or she shall be punished by imprisonment for a period of five years.
SECTION 1 (amending O.C.G.A. 16-11-121 to 16-11-124), 16-11-124 exceptions: (3) Any sawed-off shotgun, sawed-off rifle, machine gun, dangerous weapon, bump fire stock, or silencer which has been modified or changed to the extent that it is inoperative.
